title: This was bought in Kathmandu
titleHi: यह तो काठमांडु में ख़रीदा गया
scope: The passive: perfective participle + जाना, both agreeing with the subject, in any tense and with compound verbs; को on the subject makes it masculine singular; the agent with से or के द्वारा; intransitive passives for suggestions (बैठा जाए, जाया); से + negative passive for inability; transitive and intransitive pairs (तोड़ना/टूटना, बनाना/बनना, बेचना/बिकना, धोना/धुलना); oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”, direct infinitive + शुरू करना; oblique infinitive + देना “to let”; relative-correlatives जितना … उतना, जैसा … वैसा, जिस तरह का … उस तरह का, जहाँ … वहाँ, जहाँ भी, जिधर … उधर; clause reversal and mixed pairs

vocab.en: to be made, come into being

lessons.title: बोला जाना
lessons.desc: The passive: “is spoken”, “was built”, “will be sent”

items.q: Fill the gap: “These days such sweets aren't made at home.”
items.hi: आजकल ऐसी मिठाई घर पर नहीं बनाई ___ ।
items.say: आजकल ऐसी मिठाई घर पर नहीं बनाई जाती ।
items.en: {These days}[0] such[1] sweets[2] {aren't made}[5+6+7] at home[3+4].
wrong: जाता
जाता is masculine. Both parts of the passive agree with मिठाई, feminine.
जाते
जाते is masculine plural. मिठाई is feminine.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Urdu is also spoken in this area.”
items.hi: इस इलाक़े में उर्दू भी ___ जाती है ।
items.say: इस इलाक़े में उर्दू भी बोली जाती है ।
items.en: Urdu[3] is[7] also[4] spoken[5+6] in[2] this[0] area[1].
wrong: बोला
बोला is masculine. The participle agrees with उर्दू, feminine: बोली.
बोल
Stem + जाना makes a compound verb (बोल जाना “to speak out”). The passive uses the perfective participle: बोली.
बोलया
Not a word. बोलना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is बोला, बोली, with no -y-.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These letters were sent yesterday.”
items.hi: ये चिट्ठियाँ कल ___ गईं ।
items.say: ये चिट्ठियाँ कल भेजी गईं ।
items.en: These[0] letters[1] {were sent}[3+4] yesterday[2].
wrong: भेजा
भेजा is masculine. Both parts agree with चिट्ठियाँ, feminine plural: भेजी गईं.
भेज
The passive uses the perfective participle, भेजी, not the stem.
भेजया
Not a word. भेजना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is भेजा, भेजी, with no -y-.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Fill the gap: “A new hospital will be built here next year.”
items.hi: अगले साल यहाँ एक नया अस्पताल बनाया ___ ।
items.say: अगले साल यहाँ एक नया अस्पताल बनाया जाएगा ।
items.en: A[3] new[4] hospital[5] {will be built}[6+7] here[2] {next year}[0+1].
wrong: जाएगी
जाएगी is feminine. अस्पताल is masculine.
जाएँगे
जाएँगे is plural. It is one hospital.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: यह किताब पिछले साल लिखी गई थी ।
items.a: This book was written last year.
wrong: This book was being written last year.
That would be लिखी जा रही थी.
I wrote this book last year.
That would be the active मैंने यह किताब लिखी. लिखी गई थी is passive.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Which verb means “to be spoken”?
wrong: बोल जाना
Stem + जाना makes a compound verb, बोल जाना “to speak out”. The passive is the perfective participle + जाना.
बोलना
बोलना is the active verb “to speak”.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Fill the gap: “All the luggage was taken upstairs.”
items.hi: सारा सामान ऊपर ले ___ गया ।
items.say: सारा सामान ऊपर ले जाया गया ।
items.en: All[0] the luggage[1] {was taken}[3+4+5] upstairs[2].
wrong: गया
In the passive the participle of जाना is जाया — ले जाया गया.
जाए
जाए is the subjunctive. The passive needs the participle जाया before गया.
items.why: ले जाना “to take away” has a passive too, ले जाया जाना. The participle of जाना in a passive is जाया.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Fresh fruit has been bought for the guests.”
items.hi: मेहमानों के लिए ताज़े फल ख़रीदे ___ हैं ।
items.say: मेहमानों के लिए ताज़े फल ख़रीदे गए हैं ।
items.en: Fresh[3] fruit[4] {has been bought}[5+6+7] for[1+2] the guests[0].
wrong: गई
गई is feminine. फल is masculine.
गया
गया is singular. ताज़े फल is plural here, and ख़रीदे already shows it: ख़रीदे गए.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Make this passive, leaving out the doer
items.a: यहाँ बहुत चाय पी जाती है ।
wrong: यहाँ बहुत चाय पिया जाता है ।
पिया जाता is masculine. The passive agrees with चाय, feminine: पी जाती.
यहाँ बहुत चाय पी जाती हैं ।
हैं is plural. चाय is a singular subject: है.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.
items.hi: लोग यहाँ बहुत चाय पीते हैं ।
items.say: यहाँ बहुत चाय पी जाती है ।
items.en: {A lot of}[1] tea[2] {is drunk}[3+4+5] here[0].

items.q: Fill the gap: “This town used to be kept very clean.”
items.hi: पहले यह शहर बहुत साफ़ रखा ___ था ।
items.say: पहले यह शहर बहुत साफ़ रखा जाता था ।
items.en: This[1] town[2] {used to be kept}[0+5+6+7] very[3] clean[4].
wrong: जाती
जाती is feminine. शहर is masculine.
जाते
जाते is plural. It is one town.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Shall the windows be opened?”
items.say: क्या खिड़कियाँ खोली जाएँ ?
items.en: Shall[0+3] the windows[1] {be opened}[2]?
wrong: जाए
जाए is singular. खिड़कियाँ is plural: जाएँ.
जाओ
जाओ is the तुम command. A passive suggestion takes the subjunctive: जाएँ.
items.why: The subjunctive passive makes a suggestion or request: खोली जाएँ “should be opened”.

lessons.title: मुझसे नहीं जाता
lessons.desc: Passive with को, the doer with से or के द्वारा, inability, जाया

items.q: Fill the gap: “All the windows were opened.”
items.say: सारी खिड़कियों को खोला गया ।
items.en: All[0] the windows[1+2] {were opened}[3+4].
wrong: गईं
With को after the subject the passive reverts to masculine singular: खोला गया.
गई
गई is feminine. With को the passive is masculine singular, whatever the noun.
खोलया
Not a word. खोलना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is खोला, with no -y-. The gap needs गया anyway.
items.why: If the subject takes को, the passive reverts to masculine singular (खिड़कियों को खोला गया).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Those louts were caught yesterday.”
items.hi: उन गुंडों को कल पकड़ा ___ ।
items.say: उन गुंडों को कल पकड़ा गया ।
items.en: Those[0] louts[1+2] {were caught}[4+5] yesterday[3].
wrong: गए
गए is plural. With को the passive is masculine singular: पकड़ा गया.
गई
गई is feminine. With को the passive is masculine singular.
पकड़या
Not a word. पकड़ना has a consonant stem, so its perfective is पकड़ा, with no -y-. The gap needs गया anyway.
items.why: If the subject takes को, the passive reverts to masculine singular (खिड़कियों को खोला गया).

items.q: Fill the gap: “This book was written by a famous writer.”
items.hi: यह किताब एक प्रसिद्ध लेखक ___ लिखी गई थी ।
items.say: यह किताब एक प्रसिद्ध लेखक के द्वारा लिखी गई थी ।
items.en: This[0] book[1] {was written}[7+8+9] by[5+6] a[2] famous[3] writer[4].
wrong: ने
ने marks the doer of an active perfective verb. In the passive the doer takes से or के द्वारा.
को
को would make the writer the person it was written to. The doer takes से or के द्वारा.
items.why: The doer, if mentioned, takes से or, more formally, के द्वारा. ने is never used in the passive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I can't lift such a heavy bag.”
items.hi: इतना भारी थैला मुझसे उठाया नहीं ___ ।
items.say: इतना भारी थैला मुझसे उठाया नहीं जाता ।
items.en: I[3] {can't}[5+6] lift[4] such[0] a heavy[1] bag[2].
wrong: जाती
जाती is feminine. The passive agrees with थैला, masculine.
जाते
जाते is plural. It is one bag.
items.why: A negative passive with से often means “can't (bring oneself to)”: the person takes से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I can't bear to listen to his talk.”
items.hi: ___ उसकी बातें सुनी नहीं जातीं ।
items.say: मुझसे उसकी बातें सुनी नहीं जातीं ।
items.en: I[0] {can't bear}[4+5] to listen[3] to his[1] talk[2].
wrong: मैंने
ने marks the doer of an active verb. In a passive of inability the person takes से — मुझसे.
मुझे
मुझे is the को form. Inability in the passive takes से — मुझसे.
items.why: A negative passive with से often means “can't (bring oneself to)”: the person takes से.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: बच्चों से चुप नहीं रहा गया ।
wrong: The children kept quiet.
नहीं … गया is negative: they could not.
The children were told to keep quiet.
Nothing is said or told. से with a negative passive shows inability.
items.why: Even intransitive verbs such as रहना can be used in a passive of inability.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where shall we go tonight?”
items.hi: आज रात को कहाँ ___ जाए ?
items.say: आज रात को कहाँ जाया जाए ?
items.en: Where[3] {shall we go}[4+5] tonight[0+1+2]?
wrong: गया
In this passive the participle of जाना is जाया, not गया.
जाता
The passive uses the perfective participle. For जाना that is जाया.
items.why: Some intransitive verbs have a passive too, used for suggestions. The participle of जाना there is जाया, not गया.

items.q: Make this passive, leaving out the doer
wrong: चोर को पकड़ी गई ।
With को the passive is masculine singular: पकड़ा गया.
चोर ने पकड़ा गया ।
ने is never used in the passive.
items.why: If the subject takes को, the passive reverts to masculine singular (खिड़कियों को खोला गया).
items.hi: पुलिस ने चोर को पकड़ा ।
items.say: चोर को पकड़ा गया ।
items.en: The thief[0+1] {was caught}[2+3].

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेहमानों को बग़ीचे में बिठाया गया ।
items.a: The guests were seated in the garden.
wrong: The guests sat down in the garden.
That would be the active मेहमान बग़ीचे में बैठे. बिठाया गया is the passive of बिठाना “to make sit”.
The guests will be seated in the garden.
गया is past. The future would be बिठाया जाएगा.
items.why: If the subject takes को, the passive reverts to masculine singular (खिड़कियों को खोला गया).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who broke this window?”
items.hi: यह खिड़की किसने ___ ?
items.say: यह खिड़की किसने तोड़ी ?
items.en: Who[2] broke[3] this[0] window[1]?
wrong: टूटी
टूटना is intransitive: it can't take ने. With किसने the transitive तोड़ना is needed.
तोड़ा
तोड़ा is masculine. With ने the verb agrees with खिड़की, feminine.
तोड़ाया
Not a word. The perfective of तोड़ना is तोड़ा, तोड़ी, with nothing added.
items.why: Hindi often has two verbs where English has one: intransitive टूटना “break (by itself)” and transitive तोड़ना “break (something)”. बनना, बिकना and धुलना are the intransitive partners of बनाना, बेचना and धोना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Last night a branch of a tree broke in the wind.”
items.hi: कल रात हवा से पेड़ की एक डाल ___ गई ।
items.say: कल रात हवा से पेड़ की एक डाल टूट गई ।
items.en: {Last night}[0+1] a[6] branch[7] of[5] a tree[4] broke[8+9] in the wind[2+3].
wrong: तोड़
तोड़ना is transitive: someone breaks something. The branch broke by itself — टूट गई.
टूटी
The compound verb uses the stem — टूट गई.
टूटाया
Not a word. टूटना has no -āyā form. The compound verb needs the stem टूट.
items.why: Hindi often has two verbs where English has one: intransitive टूटना “break (by itself)” and transitive तोड़ना “break (something)”. बनना, बिकना and धुलना are the intransitive partners of बनाना, बेचना and धोना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Good saris are sold in this shop.”
items.hi: इस दुकान में अच्छी साड़ियाँ ___ हैं ।
items.say: इस दुकान में अच्छी साड़ियाँ बिकती हैं ।
items.en: Good[3] saris[4] {are sold}[5+6] in[2] this[0] shop[1].
wrong: बिकता
बिकता is masculine singular. साड़ियाँ is feminine plural.
बिकते
बिकते is masculine. साड़ियाँ is feminine.
items.why: बिकना “to be sold” is the intransitive partner of बेचना. बेची जाती हैं (passive) would also be right, with more stress on the act of selling.

items.q: Which intransitive verb pairs with बनाना “to make”?
wrong: बिकना
बिकना “to be sold” pairs with बेचना “to sell”.
टूटना
टूटना “to break (by itself)” pairs with तोड़ना.
items.why: बनना “to be made, come into being” is the intransitive partner of बनाना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Clothes are washed every day in this hotel.”
items.hi: इस होटल में कपड़े रोज़ ___ हैं ।
items.say: इस होटल में कपड़े रोज़ धुलते हैं ।
items.en: Clothes[3] {are washed}[5+6] {every day}[4] in[2] this[0] hotel[1].
wrong: धुलती
धुलती is feminine. कपड़े is masculine.
धुलता
धुलता is singular. कपड़े is plural.
items.why: धुलना “to be washed” is the intransitive partner of धोना. धोए जाते हैं (passive) would also be right.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: शहर में नया पुल बन रहा है ।
items.a: A new bridge is being built in the town.
wrong: The new bridge in the town has broken.
That would be टूट गया है. बन रहा है is “is being made”.
A new bridge was built in the town.
बन रहा है is continuous: it is still being built.
items.why: Hindi often has two verbs where English has one: intransitive टूटना “break (by itself)” and transitive तोड़ना “break (something)”. बनना, बिकना and धुलना are the intransitive partners of बनाना, बेचना and धोना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Our work began yesterday.”
items.hi: हमारा काम कल शुरू ___ ।
items.say: हमारा काम कल शुरू हुआ ।
items.en: Our[0] work[1] began[3+4] yesterday[2].
wrong: हुई
हुई is feminine. काम is masculine.
हुए
हुए is plural. It is one piece of work.
items.why: शुरू होना “to begin” is intransitive. शुरू किया गया (passive) would also be right.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Not seeing its mother, the child began to cry.”
items.hi: माँ को न देखकर बच्चा रोने ___ ।
items.say: माँ को न देखकर बच्चा रोने लगा ।
items.en: {Not seeing}[2+3] its mother[0+1], the child[4] began[6] to cry[5].
wrong: लगी
लगी is feminine. लगना agrees with बच्चा, masculine.
लगे
लगे is plural. It is one child.
लगनेगा
Not a word. The future of लगना is लगेगा, built on the stem. Here the past लगा is needed.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Seeing the guest, the dog began to bark.”
items.hi: मेहमान को देखकर कुत्ता ___ लगा ।
items.say: मेहमान को देखकर कुत्ता भौंकने लगा ।
items.en: Seeing[2] the guest[0+1], the dog[3] began[5] to bark[4].
wrong: भौंकना
लगना “to begin” takes the oblique infinitive: भौंकने.
भौंकता
भौंकता is the imperfective participle. लगना “to begin” takes the oblique infinitive.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.

items.q: Fill the gap: “All the girls began to sing (a song).”
items.hi: सब लड़कियाँ गाना गाने ___ ।
items.say: सब लड़कियाँ गाना गाने लगीं ।
items.en: All[0] the girls[1] began[4] to sing[3] (a song[2]).
wrong: लगी
लगी is singular. लड़कियाँ is feminine plural: लगीं.
लगे
लगे is masculine. लड़कियाँ is feminine.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Hearing what I said, Raj began to laugh.”
items.hi: मेरी बात सुनकर ___ हँसने लगा ।
items.say: मेरी बात सुनकर राज हँसने लगा ।
items.en: Hearing[2] what I said[0+1], Raj[3] began[5] to laugh[4].
wrong: राज ने
लगना does not take ने, even in the perfective.
राज को
“To begin” with लगना takes a plain subject: राज.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita started learning the tabla this year.”
items.hi: सीता ने इस साल तबला सीखना शुरू ___ ।
items.say: सीता ने इस साल तबला सीखना शुरू किया ।
items.en: Sita[0+1] started[6+7] learning[5] the tabla[4] {this year}[2+3].
wrong: की
की is feminine. Nothing here is feminine: तबला सीखना is masculine.
हुआ
शुरू होना is intransitive and takes no ने. With सीता ने the verb is शुरू किया.
items.why: Direct infinitive + शुरू करना is also “to begin to”, often deliberate. It takes ने in the perfective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Now everyone should start reading.”
items.hi: अब सब लोग ___ शुरू करें ।
items.say: अब सब लोग पढ़ना शुरू करें ।
items.en: Now[0] everyone[1+2] {should start}[4+5] reading[3].
wrong: पढ़ने
शुरू करना takes the direct infinitive, पढ़ना. The oblique पढ़ने goes with लगना.
पढ़ते
पढ़ते is the imperfective participle. शुरू करना takes the infinitive.
items.why: Direct infinitive + शुरू करना is also “to begin to”, often deliberate. It takes ने in the perfective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mother let the children play outside.”
items.hi: माँ ने बच्चों को बाहर ___ दिया ।
items.say: माँ ने बच्चों को बाहर खेलने दिया ।
items.en: Mother[0+1] let[6] the children[2+3] play[5] outside[4].
wrong: खेलना
देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive: खेलने दिया.
खेलते
खेलते is the imperfective participle. देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + देना “to let, allow”. देना takes ने in the perfective, and it agrees with a direct object unless the object takes को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “She let me read her old letters.”
items.hi: उसने मुझे अपनी पुरानी चिट्ठियाँ पढ़ने ___ ।
items.say: उसने मुझे अपनी पुरानी चिट्ठियाँ पढ़ने दीं ।
items.en: She[0] let[6] me[1] read[5] her[2] old[3] letters[4].
wrong: दिए
दिए is masculine. देना agrees with the direct object चिट्ठियाँ, feminine plural: दीं.
दी
दी is singular. चिट्ठियाँ is plural, and the nasal goes on the last word: दीं.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + देना “to let, allow”. देना takes ने in the perfective, and it agrees with a direct object unless the object takes को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Let him come in.”
items.hi: उसे अंदर ___ दो ।
items.say: उसे अंदर आने दो ।
items.en: Let[3] him[0] come[2] in[1].
wrong: आना
देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive: आने दो.
आता
आता is the imperfective participle. देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + देना “to let, allow”. देना takes ने in the perfective, and it agrees with a direct object unless the object takes को.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Don't let the children go near the fire.”
items.hi: बच्चों को आग के पास मत ___ दो ।
items.say: बच्चों को आग के पास मत जाने दो ।
items.en: Don't[5] let[7] the children[0+1] go[6] near[3+4] the fire[2].
wrong: जाना
देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive: जाने दो.
गए
गए is the perfective. देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive: जाने.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + देना “to let, allow”. देना takes ने in the perfective, and it agrees with a direct object unless the object takes को.

items.q: Which sentence means “The guests began to eat”?
wrong: मेहमानों ने खाना खाने लगे ।
लगना never takes ने — मेहमान … लगे.
मेहमान खाना खाना लगे ।
लगना “to begin” takes the oblique infinitive — खाने.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.
items.say: मेहमान खाना खाने लगे ।
items.en: The guests[0] began[3] to eat[1+2].

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: रात को मुझे डर लगने लगा ।
items.a: At night I began to feel afraid.
wrong: At night I was afraid to start.
लगने लगा is “began to be felt”: डर लगना + लगना “to begin”.
At night I began to frighten people.
डर लगना is “to feel fear”. The person who feels it takes को.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I will eat as much food as I can eat. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं ___ खाना खा सकता हूँ, उतना खाऊँगा ।
items.say: मैं जितना खाना खा सकता हूँ, उतना खाऊँगा ।
items.en: I[0] {will eat}[7] {as much}[1+6] food[2] as I {can}[4+5] eat[3]. (a man speaking)
wrong: कितना
कितना is the question word “how much?”. The relative begins with j-, जितना.
उतना
उतना is the correlative, which picks up the relative in the second clause.
items.why: जितना … उतना “as much … as”. Both agree like adjectives with what they describe.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I don't have as many books as you do.”
items.hi: जितनी किताबें तुम्हारे पास हैं, ___ मेरे पास नहीं हैं ।
items.say: जितनी किताबें तुम्हारे पास हैं, उतनी मेरे पास नहीं हैं ।
items.en: I[6+7] {don't have}[8+9] {as many}[0+5] books[1] as you[2+3] {do}[4].
wrong: उतना
उतना is masculine singular. The correlative agrees with किताबें, feminine plural: उतनी.
जितनी
जितनी is the relative. The second clause takes the correlative उतनी.
items.why: जितना … उतना “as much … as”. Both agree like adjectives with what they describe.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Do as I say. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: जैसा मैं कहता हूँ, ___ करो ।
items.say: जैसा मैं कहता हूँ, वैसा करो ।
items.en: Do[5] as[0+4] I[1] say[2+3]. (a man speaking)
wrong: कैसा
कैसा is the question word “what kind?”. The correlative begins with v-, वैसा.
जैसा
जैसा opens the relative clause. The second clause takes the correlative वैसा.
items.why: जैसा … वैसा “as … so” describes kind or manner. जिस तरह का … उस तरह का and जिस तरह (से) … उस तरह (से) are alternatives.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I want a sari like the one Sita wore too.”
items.hi: ___ साड़ी सीता ने पहनी थी, वैसी मुझे भी चाहिए ।
items.say: जैसी साड़ी सीता ने पहनी थी, वैसी मुझे भी चाहिए ।
items.en: I[7] want[9] a sari[1] like[0+6] the one Sita[2+3] wore[4+5] too[8].
wrong: जैसा
जैसा is masculine. It agrees with साड़ी, feminine: जैसी.
जैसे
जैसे is masculine plural or oblique. साड़ी is feminine singular.
items.why: जैसा … वैसा “as … so” describes kind or manner. जिस तरह का … उस तरह का and जिस तरह (से) … उस तरह (से) are alternatives.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where you go, I will go too (lit. “… there …”). (a man speaking)”
items.hi: ___ तुम जाओगे, वहाँ मैं भी जाऊँगा ।
items.say: जहाँ तुम जाओगे, वहाँ मैं भी जाऊँगा ।
items.en: Where[0] you[1] go[2], I[4] {will go}[6] too[5] (lit. “… there[3] …”). (a man speaking)
wrong: कहाँ
कहाँ is the question word “where?”. The relative begins with j-, जहाँ.
वहाँ
वहाँ is the correlative “there”, which opens the second clause.
जहाँओं
Not a word. जहाँ never changes.
items.why: जहाँ … वहाँ “where … there”, जहाँ भी “wherever”, जिधर … उधर “whither … thither”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Wherever you go, take care of yourself.”
items.hi: जहाँ ___ जाओ, अपना ध्यान रखना ।
items.say: जहाँ भी जाओ, अपना ध्यान रखना ।
items.en: Wherever[0+1] you go[2], {take care of}[4+5] yourself[3].
wrong: तक
जहाँ तक is “as far as”. “Wherever” is जहाँ भी.
से
जहाँ से is “from where”. “Wherever” is जहाँ भी.
items.why: जहाँ … वहाँ “where … there”, जहाँ भी “wherever”, जिधर … उधर “whither … thither”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Wherever you look, there are crowds of people.”
items.hi: ___ देखो, उधर लोग ही लोग हैं ।
items.say: जिधर देखो, उधर लोग ही लोग हैं ।
items.en: Wherever[0] you look[1], there[2] are[6] crowds of people[3+4+5].
wrong: किधर
किधर is the question word “whereabouts?”. The relative is जिधर.
इधर
इधर is “here, over here”. The relative is जिधर.
जिधरों
Not a word. जिधर never changes.
items.why: जहाँ … वहाँ “where … there”, जहाँ भी “wherever”, जिधर … उधर “whither … thither”.

items.q: Which sentence says the same, with the clauses reversed?
items.a: वहाँ बहुत अमीर लोग आते हैं जहाँ सीता काम करती है ।
wrong: जहाँ बहुत अमीर लोग आते हैं, वहाँ सीता काम करती है ।
This changes the meaning: “Sita works wherever lots of rich people come”.
वहाँ बहुत अमीर लोग आते हैं कहाँ सीता काम करती है ।
कहाँ is the question word. The relative is जहाँ.
items.why: The two clauses can be swapped round, correlative clause first, without changing the meaning.
items.hi: जहाँ सीता काम करती है, वहाँ बहुत अमीर लोग आते हैं ।
items.say: वहाँ बहुत अमीर लोग आते हैं जहाँ सीता काम करती है ।
items.en: {Lots of}[1] rich[2] people[3] come[4+5] there[0] where[6] Sita[7] works[8+9+10].

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जितना पैसा राज कमाता है, उतना मैं नहीं कमाता ।
items.a: I don't earn as much money as Raj does.
wrong: Raj doesn't earn as much money as I do.
नहीं goes with मैं … कमाता, it is I who earn less.
I earn as much money as Raj does.
नहीं makes it negative: not as much.
items.why: जितना … उतना “as much … as”. Both agree like adjectives with what they describe.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जैसा तुम कहोगे, वैसा ही होगा ।
items.a: It will be just as you say.
wrong: How will it be, do you think?
That would be a question with कैसा. जैसा … वैसा is “as … so”.
Whatever happens, you will talk about it.
जैसा … वैसा compares manner: things will happen the way you say.
items.why: जैसा … वैसा “as … so” describes kind or manner. जिस तरह का … उस तरह का and जिस तरह (से) … उस तरह (से) are alternatives.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Nobody cooks the way that Mother cooks.”
items.hi: ___ तरह से माँ खाना बनाती हैं, उस तरह से कोई नहीं बनाता ।
items.say: जिस तरह से माँ खाना बनाती हैं, उस तरह से कोई नहीं बनाता ।
items.en: Nobody[10+11] cooks[12] {the way}[7+8+9] that[0+1+2] Mother[3] cooks[4+5+6].
wrong: किस
किस तरह is the question “in what way?”. The relative is जिस तरह.
उस
उस तरह is the correlative, which comes in the second clause.
items.why: जैसा … वैसा “as … so” describes kind or manner. जिस तरह का … उस तरह का and जिस तरह (से) … उस तरह (से) are alternatives.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I too like clothes of the kind that Sita wears (lit. “… clothes …”).”
items.hi: जिस तरह ___ कपड़े सीता पहनती है, उस तरह के कपड़े मुझे भी पसंद हैं ।
items.say: जिस तरह के कपड़े सीता पहनती है, उस तरह के कपड़े मुझे भी पसंद हैं ।
items.en: I[11] too[12] like[13+14] clothes[10] {of the kind}[7+8+9] that[0+1+2] Sita[4] wears[5+6] (lit. “… clothes[3] …”).
wrong: का
का is masculine singular. It agrees with कपड़े, plural: के.
की
की is feminine. कपड़े is masculine.
items.why: जैसा … वैसा “as … so” describes kind or manner. जिस तरह का … उस तरह का and जिस तरह (से) … उस तरह (से) are alternatives.

items.en: These[0] shoes[1] {were made}[4+5] in Agra[2+3].
wrong: बनाई
बनाई is feminine. The passive agrees with जूते, masculine plural: बनाए गए.
बना
The passive uses the perfective participle of बनाना — बनाए.

items.en: Tea[2] {is made}[3+4+5] every[0] evening[1].
wrong: बनाया
बनाया is masculine. चाय is feminine: बनाई जाती.
जाता
जाता is masculine. Both parts agree with चाय — बनाई जाती.

items.en: The children[0+1] {were sent}[3+4] to school[2].
wrong: गए
With को after the subject the passive is masculine singular: भेजा गया.
भेजे
भेजे गए would be right without को (बच्चे स्कूल भेजे गए). With बच्चों को the passive is masculine singular.

items.en: This[0] poem[1] {was written}[5+6] by[3+4] Sita[2].
wrong: ने
ने is never used in the passive. The doer takes के द्वारा or से.
लिखा
लिखा is masculine. The passive agrees with कविता, feminine.

items.en: Raj[0+1] {couldn't}[3+4] {get up}[2].
wrong: ने
Inability in the passive takes से, not ने.
उठी
उठी is feminine. The passive of an intransitive verb is masculine singular: उठा गया.

items.en: Seeing[1] me[0], Sita[2] began[4] to laugh[3].
wrong: हँसना
लगना “to begin” takes the oblique infinitive: हँसने.
लगा
लगा is masculine. सीता is a woman: लगी.
हँसनेगा
Not a word. लगना “to begin” follows the oblique infinitive हँसने.

items.en: Grandma[0+1] let[5] me[2] go[4] to Delhi[3].
wrong: जाना
देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive — जाने.
दी
दी is feminine. There is no direct object here, so दिया.
देनेगा
Not a word. The future of देना is देगा. Here the past is needed — दिया.

items.en: Mohan[0+1] started[4+5] cooking[2+3].
wrong: बनाने
शुरू करना takes the direct infinitive — बनाना शुरू किया.
हुआ
शुरू होना is intransitive and takes no ने. With मोहन ने it is शुरू किया.

items.en: There aren't[7+8] {as many}[0+5] trees[1] here[6] as {there are}[4] {in the village}[2+3].
wrong: कितने
कितने is the question word. The relative is जितने.
उतना
उतना is singular. The correlative agrees with पेड़, here plural: उतने.

items.en: Do[6] just[5] as[0+4] Mother[1] says[2+3].
wrong: कैसा
कैसा is the question word. The relative is जैसा.
कहता
कहता is masculine. माँ is a woman, and respect makes it plural: कहती हैं.

items.en: Wherever[1+2] we[0] went[3], we[5] got[8] good[6] food[7] (lit. “… there[4] …”).
wrong: कहाँ
कहाँ is the question word. “Wherever” is जहाँ भी.
हमने
मिलना takes no ने — the receiver takes को, हमें.

items.en: My[0] cup[1] broke[2+3].
wrong: तोड़
तोड़ना is transitive: someone breaks something. The cup broke by itself: टूट गया.
गई
गई is feminine. प्याला is masculine.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: यह फ़िल्म बच्चों को नहीं दिखाई जाएगी ।
items.a: This film won't be shown to children.
wrong: The children won't show this film.
बच्चों को is “to the children”. दिखाई जाएगी is passive: the film will be shown.
This film wasn't shown to children.
जाएगी is future: “won't be shown”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: बच्चे खेलने लगे और बड़े बातें करने लगे ।
items.a: The children began to play and the grown-ups began to talk.
wrong: The children let the grown-ups play and talk.
“Let” would be देना. लगना with the oblique infinitive is “begin to”.
The children played and the grown-ups talked.
लगे adds “began to”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मुझे सोने दो !
wrong: I have to sleep!
“Have to” would be मुझे सोना है. सोने दो is “let (me) sleep”.
I'm beginning to fall asleep!
“Begin to” is लगना. देना with the oblique infinitive is “let”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जितना काम आज हुआ, उतना पूरे हफ़्ते में नहीं हुआ ।
items.a: Not as much work got done in the whole week as got done today.
wrong: As much work got done today as in the whole week.
नहीं हुआ makes the second clause negative.
Less work got done today than in the whole week.
It is the other way round: the week saw less work than today.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: जहाँ पहले तालाब था, वहाँ अब एक बड़ा होटल है ।
items.a: Where there used to be a pond, there's now a big hotel.
wrong: There's now a big hotel next to the pond.
जहाँ … वहाँ is “where … there”: the hotel stands where the pond was.
Where is the big hotel that used to be by the pond?
जहाँ is the relative “where”, not a question.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: दुकान में घटिया सामान बेचा जा रहा था ।
items.a: Inferior goods were being sold in the shop.
wrong: Fine goods were being sold in the shop.
घटिया means “inferior, low grade”.
Inferior goods will be sold in the shop.
जा रहा था is past continuous: “were being sold”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: उस बेचारे से बोला नहीं गया ।
wrong: Nobody spoke to the poor fellow.
से with a negative passive shows inability: he could not speak.
The poor fellow wasn't told.
“Told” would be बताया. बोला गया is from बोलना “to speak”.

lessons.title: Rules and usage
lessons.desc: The passive, लगना, देना and relatives

items.q: The Hindi passive is made of …
wrong: the verb stem + जाना
Stem + जाना makes a compound verb (बोल जाना “to speak out”).
the imperfective participle + जाना
The passive uses the perfective participle: बोला जाना.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense.

items.q: In a passive sentence, what does the verb agree with?
items.a: The subject, unless it takes को
wrong: The doer, marked with से or के द्वारा
The doer is often not mentioned, and the verb never agrees with it.
Always masculine singular, as after को
Only when the subject takes को. Otherwise both parts agree with the subject.
items.why: The passive is the perfective participle + जाना (बोला जाना “to be spoken”). Both parts agree with the subject, in any tense. If the subject takes को, the passive reverts to masculine singular (खिड़कियों को खोला गया).

items.q: In the passive, the doer of the action takes …
wrong: ने
ने is never used in the passive.
को
को on the subject makes the passive masculine singular. The doer takes से or के द्वारा.
items.why: The doer, if mentioned, takes से or, more formally, के द्वारा. ने is never used in the passive.

items.q: What does a negative passive with से often suggest?
wrong: A polite request
Requests use the subjunctive passive, e.g. खोली जाएँ.
A planned action
Planned action is more typical of शुरू करना or the infinitive + होना.
items.why: A negative passive with से often means “can't (bring oneself to)”: the person takes से.

items.q: लगना “to begin to” takes …
items.a: the oblique infinitive, and never ने
wrong: the direct infinitive, with ने in the perfective
That describes शुरू करना.
the oblique infinitive, with ने in the perfective
That describes देना “to let”. लगना never takes ने.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + लगना “to begin to”. लगना takes no ने, and it agrees with its subject.

items.q: देना “to let, allow” takes …
items.a: the oblique infinitive, and ने in the perfective
wrong: the oblique infinitive, but never ने
देना is transitive: उसने मुझे जाने दिया.
the direct infinitive, like शुरू करना
देना “to let” takes the oblique infinitive: जाने दो.
items.why: Oblique infinitive + देना “to let, allow”. देना takes ने in the perfective, and it agrees with a direct object unless the object takes को.

items.q: In कहाँ जाया जाए ? why is it जाया and not गया?
items.a: In the passive the participle of जाना is जाया
wrong: जाया is the subjunctive of जाना
The subjunctive is जाए. जाया is the participle used only in the passive.
जाया is a dialect form of गया
It is standard: the passive of जाना always uses जाया.
items.why: Some intransitive verbs have a passive too, used for suggestions. The participle of जाना there is जाया, not गया.

items.q: बेची जाती हैं and बिकती हैं can both mean “are sold”. How do they differ?
items.a: The passive stresses the act of selling, बिकना things being on sale
wrong: बिकना is not used in modern Hindi
Both are everyday Hindi.
बेची जाती हैं is only used in the past
The passive can be used in any tense.
items.why: Hindi often has two verbs where English has one: intransitive टूटना “break (by itself)” and transitive तोड़ना “break (something)”. बनना, बिकना and धुलना are the intransitive partners of बनाना, बेचना and धोना.
